solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Major Mike at home feeding pup? (7)

indicatorNotes.feeding: M and IN are fed into the pup's parent, so they go inside SEAL

blocks.note: a pup is a young seal, so the question mark lets 'pup' stand for the animal
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
at home = in

annotation.surface: An army major is at home feeding the family puppy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Major' reads as a rank and 'pup' as a dog, but the pup is a seal's, and 'major' is the adjective meaning highly important.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its figurative sense: a work that seeds later ones is major, highly influential.

entries.clue: Put an end to row involving stray animal (6,7)

indicatorNotes.involving: the row involves, i.e. surrounds, the word for stray

blocks.note: to scotch a rumour is to put an end to it
a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

annotation.surface: Someone intervenes to stop a quarrel over a stray animal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'row' a quarrel and 'stray' an adjective for the animal; here row is a line and stray is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this Scottish breed of dog is one kind of animal, the broadest possible hint.

entries.clue: Claims uniform lost in play? (7)

indicatorNotes.lost: letters that are lost are all at sea, so they come out in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A critic complains that the uniform stated claims get lost in the plot of a play.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a musical is one kind of play with songs.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show, a kind of play with music.

entries.clue: A lack of dotted letters on electronic report (5)

blocks.note: no = a lack of, as in 'no money'
the letter i is dotted, so dotted letters are I's
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

annotation.surface: Someone complains that an electronic report is missing its dots over the letters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a document, but it is the sound of a gun: a report is a loud bang.
annotation.definitionFit: A report is a loud noise, such as a gunshot.

entries.clue: Game friend climbing across English river in mist (8)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the word for friend reads upwards
indicatorNotes.across: the reversed friend stretches across E, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.in: R sits in the word for mist

blocks.note: pal = friend, reversed to LAP
E = English
fog = mist
R = river

annotation.surface: A game in which a friend climbs across an English river in the mist.
annotation.walkthrough: LAP goes round E to make LEAP, and FOG goes round R to make FROG.
annotation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game of vaulting over one another's backs.

entries.clue: Spot bladed tool after son’s gone for papa (6)

indicatorNotes.gone for: the S has gone and P has come in for it

blocks.note: a sickle is a curved bladed tool
S = son, the letter taken out
Papa is P in the NATO alphabet, the letter put in

annotation.surface: Someone notices a bladed tool after the son has left, to be replaced by his father.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is a tricky situation, as in 'a spot of bother'; being in a pickle means the same.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'in a spot' and 'in a pickle' both mean in trouble, so the two nouns match.

entries.clue: Small hole for Dr Spooner’s birdie (6)

indicatorNotes.Dr Spooner’s: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words for small hole swap their starts

blocks.note: wee = small; it takes the P from the second word
a pit is a hole; it takes the W from the first word

annotation.surface: A golfing line: a small hole gives a birdie.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is golf, where a birdie is a score; here it is a small bird. The peewit, or lapwing, is named for its call.
annotation.definitionFit: The peewit is a bird, and birdie is a playful word for a bird.

entries.clue: Clicking instruments scan state in chaos (9)

indicatorNotes.in chaos: the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Clicking instruments scan a country thrown into chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clicking' suggests a computer mouse and 'scan' a machine, pulling the mind toward technology rather than a Spanish dancer's hands.
annotation.definitionFit: Castanets are handheld percussion instruments that click together.

entries.clue: Trouble rearing child after one’s affair (7)

indicatorNotes.rearing: a horse rearing rises up, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble, reversed to LIA
one = I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'has', joining the parts
a son is a child

annotation.surface: Someone's affair has brought trouble in the form of raising a child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rearing child' looks like parenting, but rearing turns the trouble upside down; the child comes after I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the romantic sense: an illicit relationship is called an affair or a liaison.

entries.clue: Hard to shift some fake tan: it’s bottled on the counter (9)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters are used
indicatorNotes.on the counter: counter means against, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: faKE TAN ITS BOttled, read backwards

annotation.surface: A shop complaint: fake tan sold in bottles over the counter is hard to wash off.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'hard to shift' a stubborn stain and 'on the counter' a shop; both are about the letters instead.
annotation.definitionFit: An obstinate person is stubborn, hard to shift from a position.

entries.clue: Trophy hunters bivouac at last on side of mountain (5)

indicatorNotes.at last: take the last letter of each word

blocks.note: last letters of hunterS bivouaC
an alp is a high pasture on a mountainside

annotation.surface: Trophy hunters camp out overnight on a mountainside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trophy hunters' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Trophy' alone; a scalp was taken as a trophy of victory.
annotation.definitionFit: A scalp was taken from a defeated enemy as a trophy, and still means a prize or victory.

entries.clue: Staff patrolling study detect odour from youth (13)

indicatorNotes.patrolling: the staff patrols round the study, so POLE goes around READ

blocks.note: a pole is a staff
to read a subject is to study it
to scent is to detect by smell

annotation.surface: Staff on patrol in a study notice a smell coming from a young person.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests school staff and a smelly teenager; 'staff' is a stick and 'study' a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A preadolescent is a child just before the teenage years, a youth.

entries.clue: Cold hair on face after temperature drops in store (5)

indicatorNotes.drops: the T is dropped from the word for facial hair

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
tache is British slang for a moustache
T = temperature, the letter dropped

annotation.surface: A man with a moustache feels the cold when the temperature drops in a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: C comes first, then TACHE loses its T to leave ACHE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hidden stock of supplies, or a computer's fast memory, is a store.

entries.clue: Charlie stuffing grass inside iron dish (9)

indicatorNotes.stuffing: Charlie is stuffed into the grass
indicatorNotes.inside: the whole lot goes inside the symbol for iron

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
rice is a grass
a charlie is a fool, as in 'a right charlie', so an ass

annotation.surface: Someone called Charlie stuffs grass into an iron dish.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie is not the NATO C here: 'a right charlie' is British for a fool. The surface serves grass in an iron dish, but the dish is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a dish of meat stewed in a white sauce.

entries.clue: Fundraiser in hotel sadly wrapped up by 22.00 (8)

indicatorNotes.sadly: the letters of hotel are in a sorry state, so rearranged
indicatorNotes.wrapped up by: the rearranged letters go inside TEN

blocks.note: 22.00 is ten o'clock at night
anagram of HOTEL

annotation.surface: A fundraising event held in a hotel sadly has to finish by ten at night.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram gives only five of the eight letters; TEN wraps around them.
annotation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity.

entries.clue: Quarter of maidens within Italian city run (9)

indicatorNotes.within: M goes within the name of the city

blocks.note: Trieste is a port in north-east Italy
M = maiden (over) in cricket scoring
R = run in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A cricket report: a quarter of the maiden overs came in an Italian city, plus a run.
annotation.walkthrough: In American colleges a quarter is an academic term, and so is a trimester, though a trimester is a third of the year.
annotation.definitionFit: Both a quarter and a trimester are divisions of the academic year.

entries.clue: Tip from head following a drink (6)

indicatorNotes.following: the tip of the head comes after the word for a

blocks.note: per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
a nod is a tip of the head

annotation.surface: Someone gets a tip-off from the boss after a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice or a gratuity; it is a small tilt of the head.
annotation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit.

entries.clue: American egoists periodically forward fake news? (8)

blocks.note: A = American
the even letters of eGoIsTs
a prop is a forward in rugby

annotation.surface: Self-centred Americans keep passing on fake news.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a verb for passing on a message; it is a rugby position. The question mark admits agitprop is political propaganda, not necessarily false.
annotation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, which the setter wryly likens to fake news.

entries.clue: Quail on centre of Delacroix painting (6)

indicatorNotes.centre of: take the middle letter of the name

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
the middle letter of DelaCroix
an oil is a painting

annotation.surface: A quail sits at the centre of a Delacroix painting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quail' reads as the game bird in a painting; it is the verb meaning to flinch.
annotation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, to recoil.

entries.clue: Half-rotated solid shape completely white (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Half-rotated: only half the word is turned round: the second half of CUBE flips

blocks.note: a cube is a solid shape; its second half BE becomes EB
all = completely, as in 'all alone'

annotation.surface: A solid shape, turned halfway round, turns out to be entirely white.
annotation.walkthrough: In snooker and pool the cue ball is the white ball, which players simply call 'the white'.
annotation.definitionFit: A snooker and pool idiom: players call the ball struck with the cue simply 'the white'.

entries.clue: Faces of each Girl Guide female will shade (8)

indicatorNotes.Faces of: the face of a word is its front, so take first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Each Girl Guide
she'll = female will

annotation.surface: The faces of every Girl Guide will be shaded, as if a female will do it.
annotation.walkthrough: SHE'LL loses its apostrophe to become SHELL. A Girl Guide is the British equivalent of a Girl Scout.
annotation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a pale off-white shade, and also a paint finish.

entries.clue: Unusual items in books Mexican barely absorbs (7)

indicatorNotes.barely: stripped bare, the word loses its outer letters
indicatorNotes.absorbs: the stripped word takes in the books

blocks.note: MEXICAN without its outside letters
OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Strange items appear in books that a Mexican barely takes in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like 'hardly', but it means stripped bare; 'books' is the usual shorthand for the Old Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: Exotica are unusual or foreign objects, the plural of a Latin word.

entries.clue: Jack perhaps abridged pieces for opera (6)

indicatorNotes.abridged: shortened, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a jack is an example of a playing card, hence 'perhaps'; it loses its D
chess or draughts pieces are men

annotation.surface: An abridged version of Jack's parts is prepared for an opera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name, perhaps a singer; it is a card, shortened to CAR.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Bizet's 1875 tale of a Spanish gypsy is one of the best-known operas.

entries.clue: Unpolished pine leg antiquarian keeps (9)

indicatorNotes.keeps: the phrase keeps the answer within it

blocks.note: pINE LEG ANTiquarian

annotation.surface: An antiquarian dealer keeps an unvarnished pine table leg.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unpolished' reads as unvarnished wood beside the pine; it means lacking grace.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the figurative sense: lacking refinement or grace, like rough unfinished wood.

entries.clue: Fine gambling competition taking pressure off suckers (5)

indicatorNotes.taking: with off, the P is taken away
indicatorNotes.off: with taking, the P is removed

blocks.note: F = fine, on pencils
the pools are the British football pools, a betting competition
P = pressure, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A fine for a gambling competition that takes the pressure off its suckers.
annotation.walkthrough: The football pools are a long-running British betting game on match results; POOLS without its P is OOLS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sucker is a gullible person easily duped, as a fool is.

entries.clue: Dash from fiery burst escaping from trap (5)

indicatorNotes.escaping from trap: trap is slang for mouth, so the word comes out of the mouth: it is spoken

blocks.note: a flare is a sudden burst of flame

annotation.surface: Someone makes a quick dash away from a fiery explosion to escape a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a sprint, but it means style, and 'trap' is slang for mouth, so the word escaping from it is spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: Dash is stylish panache, which is flair.

entries.clue: Unfinished highway outside of skinflint’s joint? (5)

indicatorNotes.Unfinished: the word loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.outside of: the outside of a word is its skin, its first and last letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: ROAD with its last letter cut
the outer letters of SkinflinT

annotation.surface: A miser's premises stand by an unfinished road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a building or a hangout; the question mark signals a joint of meat, which a roast is.
annotation.definitionFit: A joint of meat is cooked as a roast, so a roast is one kind of joint.

entries.clue: Clobber from African country’s taken by horse (9)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the horse takes in the country's name

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
Mali's

annotation.surface: A horse is taken from an African country for a thrashing.
annotation.walkthrough: Marmalise is British slang for beating someone thoroughly, and clobber is the same.
annotation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to marmalise them, both meaning to thrash.

entries.clue: Bit part of fish covering large skinned dory (6)

indicatorNotes.covering: the fin covers, so goes around, the other letters
indicatorNotes.skinned: the fish loses its skin, its outer letters

blocks.note: a fin is part of a fish
L = large
DORY without its outer letters

annotation.surface: A small part of a fish covers a large skinned dory.
annotation.walkthrough: The florin was an old British coin worth two shillings, known as a two-bob bit; 'bit' is the coin, not a small part.
annotation.definitionFit: A bit is a coin, and the florin was the two-shilling bit.

entries.clue: Sweet old man starts to recce faraway island (7)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: pa = father, one's old man
first letters of Recce Faraway
an ait is a small river island, especially on the Thames

annotation.surface: A kind old man begins to scout out a distant island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective describing the old man; it is a noun, the British word for dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: A parfait is a frozen dessert, and sweet is British for dessert.
